answer: Each identity anchors to one registered beehive: a smart scale signs a fresh nectar-flow curve each epoch, bound to the epoch nonce and checked against RFID-tagged foragers whose spiral return flights are unique per colony. One hive casts one vote; two identities sharing one curve collapse to one vote and burn a $50 stake. A farm wanting 100 votes must buy 100 real hives, about $300 each plus $40 a year, each needing a season of logged flow — no comet-fast shortcut. No fresh signed curve means no vote, so split or pre-raised identities gain nothing and marginal cost rises linearly with n.
